decisions.title: OTLP signal and transport profile
decisions.issue: OTLP defines multiple signals, encodings, and transports while this runtime must expose a stable application profile.
interpretations: Expose every OTLP signal and encoding
Support trace and metric protobuf export over gRPC and HTTP
Delegate all transport selection to environment variables
decisions.peer_behavior: OpenTelemetry Go v1.44.0 provides separate trace and metric exporters for OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP protobuf.
decisions.selected_behavior: The stable runtime exports traces and metrics using explicitly selected OTLP/gRPC or OTLP/HTTP protobuf; logs, profiles, and OTLP/HTTP JSON are outside the profile.
decisions.rationale: The selected stable OpenTelemetry Go exporters provide one explicit vendor-neutral profile without promising unstable signals.
decisions.security_consequences: Explicit endpoints and headers avoid implicit vendor configuration.
decisions.resource_consequences: Exporter queues, batches, timeouts, and metric cardinality remain separately bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Adding another signal or encoding requires compatibility review.
decisions.wire_consequences: Trace and metric requests use the pinned OTLP protobuf service messages over the selected transport.
decisions.upstream_status: OTLP 1.10.0 is pinned and later protocol releases are monitored without automatic behavior changes.
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported OpenTelemetry Go line changes its stable OTLP signal or transport contract.

decisions.title: Bounded OTLP delivery and transport security
decisions.issue: OTLP classifies delivery failures but does not choose application timeout, retry horizon, TLS identity, or local plaintext policy.
interpretations: Use exporter defaults without validation
Require TLS for every endpoint
Require explicit bounded timeouts and retries while allowing deliberate local plaintext
decisions.peer_behavior: OpenTelemetry Go exporters implement OTLP retry classification, gzip, TLS, and per-attempt timeout options but leave policy values to callers.
decisions.selected_behavior: Exporter configuration requires a positive timeout, finite retry intervals when enabled, coherent TLS material, and rejects combining plaintext with TLS settings; plaintext remains an explicit local or same-cluster option.
decisions.rationale: Fail-closed validation prevents contradictory security identity and unbounded retry policy while retaining practical Collector deployment.
decisions.security_consequences: TLS identity and client credentials cannot be silently ignored by plaintext mode.
decisions.resource_consequences: Retries and attempts have finite configured horizons and compression is limited to none or gzip.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Previously tolerated contradictory or unbounded configuration is rejected.
decisions.wire_consequences: Retryable OTLP failures may be retried within the configured horizon; non-retryable and timed-out attempts surface exporter errors.
decisions.upstream_status: OTLP retry and throttling rules are monitored separately from package deployment policy.
decisions.reconsider_when: OTLP or OpenTelemetry Go defines incompatible mandatory client delivery or security behavior.

decisions.title: Bounded W3C Trace Context extraction
decisions.section: 3 traceparent Header Field and 3.2 tracestate Header Field
decisions.issue: Trace Context defines parsing and invalid-field behavior but does not set one combined application allocation budget for traceparent and tracestate.
interpretations: Parse headers without a package bound
Reject the containing request when propagation is malformed
Ignore propagation when the combined configured byte bound is exceeded
decisions.peer_behavior: OpenTelemetry Go v1.44.0 TraceContext parses the W3C fields and ignores invalid context without returning an application error.
decisions.selected_behavior: Extraction delegates W3C syntax and version handling to OpenTelemetry Go only when traceparent plus tracestate fit the configured positive byte bound; malformed or oversized context is ignored without failing the carrier operation.
decisions.rationale: Distributed context remains interoperable while hostile metadata cannot force unbounded parsing or application failure.
decisions.security_consequences: Invalid or oversized context grants no remote parent authority.
decisions.resource_consequences: Combined trace-context header work is bounded before peer parsing.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Peers sending context beyond the configured budget lose trace linkage.
decisions.wire_consequences: Valid in-budget traceparent and tracestate retain OpenTelemetry Go W3C semantics.
decisions.upstream_status: The 2021 Recommendation and W3C publication history are monitored.
decisions.reconsider_when: A superseding Trace Context Recommendation changes field processing or mandatory limits.

decisions.title: Outbound W3C propagation replaces stale fields
decisions.issue: Carrier APIs may already contain traceparent, tracestate, or baggage values and append-versus-replace behavior can create ambiguous downstream context.
interpretations: Append to existing fields
Leave stale fields when the current context has no value
Clear owned fields before injecting one current context
decisions.peer_behavior: OpenTelemetry Go v1.44.0 serializes one current TraceContext value through TextMapCarrier.Set.
decisions.selected_behavior: Injection clears traceparent, tracestate, and baggage before writing the filtered current context, so stale carrier values never survive or concatenate.
decisions.rationale: One outbound request must carry at most one unambiguous package-owned propagation profile.
decisions.security_consequences: Attacker-supplied stale context cannot remain alongside current authority.
decisions.resource_consequences: Replacement keeps carrier growth constant across retries and clones.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Callers relying on prepopulated propagation values must provide them through the current context.
decisions.wire_consequences: Outbound propagation contains only the current serialized W3C fields and filtered baggage.
decisions.upstream_status: No W3C erratum selecting append semantics is known; publication history is monitored.
decisions.reconsider_when: TextMapCarrier or Trace Context defines conflicting multi-value injection semantics.

decisions.title: Trusted allow-listed baggage profile
decisions.section: 3.3.2 Limits, 3.5 Mutating Baggage, and 4 Security Considerations
decisions.issue: The Candidate Recommendation encourages propagation and defines minimum compliant capacity, while arbitrary baggage can cross trust boundaries, leak data, and create cardinality or allocation pressure.
interpretations: Propagate every valid member up to W3C limits
Disable all baggage permanently
Disable baggage by default and require a trusted boundary, allow-list, item limit, and byte limit
decisions.peer_behavior: OpenTelemetry Go v1.44.0 implements W3C baggage grammar; it does not choose this package's trust boundary or application allow-list.
decisions.selected_behavior: Untrusted extraction always clears baggage. Trusted extraction and injection are opt-in, retain only allow-listed keys, enforce configured positive item and byte bounds, and drop oversized output rather than emitting partial members.
decisions.rationale: The profile deliberately prioritizes privacy and bounded authority over transparent propagation and does not claim full Candidate Recommendation propagation compliance.
decisions.security_consequences: Unknown keys, user identifiers, secrets, and untrusted baggage do not cross the package boundary by default.
decisions.resource_consequences: Parsed and emitted baggage is bounded by configured bytes and item count.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: General W3C baggage peers can observe dropped members; trusted applications must declare their stable key contract.
decisions.wire_consequences: The baggage header is absent unless enabled and contains only complete allow-listed members within bounds.
decisions.upstream_status: The 2024 document remains a Candidate Recommendation and its W3C history is monitored.
decisions.reconsider_when: Baggage reaches Recommendation with incompatible security, limits, or mutation requirements.

decisions.title: Owned resource identity and schema version
decisions.section: Resource service, deployment environment, and telemetry SDK attributes
decisions.issue: Semantic conventions define resource keys but do not decide whether generic caller attributes may replace runtime-owned service and SDK identity.
interpretations: Let generic attributes override every key
Silently prefer whichever detector runs last
Reserve owned identity keys and attach the v1.40.0 schema URL
decisions.peer_behavior: OpenTelemetry Go v1.44.0 exposes generated v1.40.0 resource keys and SchemaURL while leaving merge precedence to the application.
decisions.selected_behavior: BuildResource owns service, deployment environment, telemetry SDK identity, and the v1.40.0 schema URL; generic Resource entries cannot override reserved keys and other bounded custom attributes remain available.
decisions.rationale: Stable service identity cannot depend on map order or attacker-controlled generic attributes.
decisions.security_consequences: Caller-supplied generic attributes cannot impersonate the configured service or SDK.
decisions.resource_consequences: Custom attribute count and value sizes remain bounded by configuration validation.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Changing the semantic-convention schema or reserved identity set requires resource compatibility review.
decisions.wire_consequences: Exported resources carry the pinned schema URL and deterministic service and SDK attributes.
decisions.upstream_status: Semantic Conventions 1.40.0 and later releases are monitored without automatic schema migration.
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported OpenTelemetry Go release requires a different stable resource schema or merge contract.

decisions.title: Privacy-minimized semantic instrumentation profile
decisions.section: HTTP, database, messaging, and general error semantic conventions
decisions.issue: Semantic conventions define broad signal attributes while stable library instrumentation must choose a bounded subset and avoid payload, target, credential, and high-cardinality data.
interpretations: Emit every available semantic attribute
Use custom names only
Emit stable low-cardinality semantic keys plus bounded package-specific metrics and omit sensitive values
decisions.peer_behavior: OpenTelemetry maintained instrumentations commonly emit richer protocol and network attributes; this package uses the same stable key vocabulary for its smaller owned profile.
decisions.selected_behavior: HTTP, PostgreSQL, queue, and cache instrumentation emits fixed operation, route-template, status-class, system, and error-class attributes plus bounded package metrics; it excludes raw paths, queries, hosts, headers, addresses, SQL, arguments, keys, messages, errors, and panic values.
decisions.rationale: Semantic interoperability does not require collecting sensitive or unbounded data that the package cannot safely govern.
decisions.security_consequences: Default telemetry omits payloads, credentials, raw identifiers, and error text.
decisions.resource_consequences: Attribute domains and metric cardinality remain bounded by fixed enums, configured allow-lists, and cardinality limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Consumers receive a documented subset rather than every attribute emitted by broader maintained instrumentations.
decisions.wire_consequences: OTLP attributes use stable semantic keys where selected and package-specific names for explicitly owned metrics.
decisions.upstream_status: Semantic Convention stability and release changes are monitored independently from package privacy policy.
decisions.reconsider_when: A stable required semantic attribute conflicts with the package privacy or cardinality contract.
